newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee claws back from lows, spreads active.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee claws back from lows, spreads active.

text.p: Robusta coffee futures recovered on Monday afternoon with the key Nov/Jan spread attracting most market attention in heavy trading volumes, market sources said. "People have been concentrating on the spreads...they're aligning their positions," said one trader.

The key Nov/Jan switch, a barometer of nearby availability, widened to $113 at the close but traders said further gains were unlikely as the spread would now draw in fresh coffee. "November is where the roaster buying is and the fund selling is in the January, so that's keeping the spread at the level -- apart from the underlying fundamental issues," he said.
Earlier in the session, trade and origin selling depressed values while the price downtrend continued to scare buyers away.
At the close, November stood $6 lower at $1,500 after touching a session low of $1,482. January was down $12 at $1,387 and overall volume reached a hefty 9,113 lots.
Bullish crop news from central America where Hurricane Lili has pounded many farm lands went largely ignored by players who said the extent of the damage on coffee was overestimated.
"The rains may delay the crop a little bit, but it's not a major factor. I think farmers are just trying to cushion the market up," said one trader.

Lili's latest casualty was Cuba where losses were reported mainly in sugar and fruits. Some coffee area was also affected. In its latest Commodity Market Trends report, broker Merrill Lynch said coffee supplies were not expected to emerge for at least another month, although the 1996/97 crop year had officially started.
